steps: Agree the tables with your data team, confirm change tracking is on for each one, and record keys and owners in a table inventory.
Create the relational schema for each table, with a primary key and a version, plus a timestamp for event data.
Set up the Experience Platform source with change data capture (Data Mirror), map the fields and set the sync schedule.
Add the synced datasets to your Customer Journey Analytics connection with their join, and add their fields to the data view.
Reconcile record counts against the warehouse for an agreed day, and check that an update and a delete arrive after the next sync.
deliverables: Synced datasets in the CJA connection and data view
asks: A data team contact who can confirm change tracking and grant access to the agreed tables
The list of tables, and the person ID they share with your other data
risk: Records that do not join to web activity: we agree the shared ID first and test the match rate on a sample before the full sync.
outcome: Your warehouse tables stay in step with Customer Journey Analytics, updates and deletes included, so reports read current data.

steps: Map your users by role, from report readers to analysts who build projects, and plan an onboarding path for each.
Train each group in Analysis Workspace on its own tasks, with exercises on your own data.
For users who know Adobe Analytics, cover the key differences, which Adobe advises giving three to six months to learn.
Set up shared components and project templates, so every team starts from agreed metrics and dimensions.
asks: The names and roles of the people to train
Time from each group for the sessions
risk: Users drifting back to old reports: we build the first shared projects with them, so their everyday questions start in Customer Journey Analytics.
outcome: Your analysts and report readers answer their own questions in Customer Journey Analytics, from shared and agreed components.

steps: Connect and curate the approved content sources for the agreed products, with your reviewers signing off each source.
Design the conversations and guardrails for the agreed questions, and configure the brand voice and the required disclosures.
Set up the handoff, by live chat, meeting booking or both, routed to one team you designate.
Build the golden-answer test set and the refusal and escalation scenarios with your reviewers, and score the answers against the agreed level.
Complete Adobe's pre-go-live checks and launch on the agreed pages in stages.
deliverables: A live Brand Concierge experience on the agreed pages
Completed pre-go-live checklist and rollout record
asks: Reviewers who approve sources, answers and disclosures
The team that receives handoffs, and its hours
risk: An answer that strays from approved content: every source is signed off, and the golden-answer set must pass before each stage goes live.
outcome: Visitors get answers drawn from your approved content, with a clear route to a person when they need one.
